path.id: A significant portion of users did not even enter the hotel funnel. This indicates low intent or lack of awareness about the stay options post-flight.
Drop-offs occur at the listing (22.4%) and detail screens (31.8%), where users are actively evaluating options.
The highest drop-off (52%) happens at the review stage, just before booking, showing hesitation at the final commitment point.
We found the WHAT, we moved on to finding the WHY behind it.....
We divided the users in two groups 1 group which was a budget user and another 1 who were premium users, we got 55 responses for budget users and 44 for premium users.
We conducted the user survey on optimal workshop, we got the IDs of the intended users , whom then we sent out the survey through our inhouse tool URT and IRIS. It was sent on Whatsapp.
8 budget users and 4 premium users were interviewed who were open th having a session after the filled survey
The interview were conducted remotely on zoom.
Avoiding users joining only for the incentives and recruiting users who could provide meaningful insights.
Same users were considered for the usability testing

The usability testing was conducted in a moderated remote format. Participants joined sessions over video conferencing platforms, where they were guided through key tasks such as booking a flight, encountering cross-sell offers, exploring hotel listings, and completing a hotel booking. Screen sharing and real-time observation allowed us to capture user behaviors, expressions, hesitations, and verbal feedback throughout the journey.
